narrative.overview:
The product is a tool for looking at elections, and it behaves like a modern tool rather than an instrument room: one sans voice, sentence-case labels, soft rounded cards, a single accent, two themes that follow the reader's system, and a shell that rearranges itself to the screen. The data is still the loudest thing on a screen, because a party's own colour is never the product's. This replaces the earlier dark-only Night Desk world; its neutral hexes, contrast floors, party-colour rules and provenance rules carry over.

The voice is forensic, calm and civic: every figure carries its source, how it was derived and what is missing; the chrome is neutral and rounded and moves only to carry state; nothing recommends, ranks or editorialises, and the one accent is for wayfinding and affordance, never for a mark.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes from one light-dark() token block, with a System / Light / Dark toggle and a pre-paint script.
One voice: the system sans, tabular numerals; monospace only for real code.
One indigo accent, the same on every page, never on a data mark.
Two radii (12px, 8px) and seven spacing steps.
Depth by theme: a soft shadow in light, a 1px ring and faint shadow in dark.
Adaptive navigation: icon rail, labelled sidebar from 1360px, bottom tab bar at 640px and below.
Motion inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference only, carrying state.

rules.name: The Data Hue Rule
rules.body: A hue on a data mark means what the data says, and nothing else. A party's colour is the party's, a ramp is a magnitude, a semantic ink is its meaning. The accent is not on this list.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is one accent hue per theme and it is the same on every page. It says where you are and what you can press, never what a mark is.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: Every ink clears 4.5:1 as text on all three surfaces, and every mark clears 3:1, in both themes. iei.test.ts holds the neutral hexes.

rules.name: The Three-Ink Rule
rules.body: Three reading inks and no fourth.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Sans for everything; tabular numerals for every figure. Never uppercase, never tracked, never monospace for a label, a figure or a tag.

rules.name: The Fluid Three Rule
rules.body: Answer, lead and title are clamp() between a phone's size and a laptop's.

rules.name: The Seven Steps Rule
rules.body: Every length is a token on the 4-8-12-16-24-32-48 scale; values off the scale are carried drift, not a licence.

rules.name: The Theme Elevation Rule
rules.body: Light separates by shadow and no border; dark separates by a ring and a faint shadow.

rules.name: The Quiet State Rule
rules.body: Hover and press change a fill or an ink, and press moves a control down 1px. They do not change a shadow.

rules.name: The Two Radii Rule
rules.body: 12px holds things, 8px is pressed. A third corner is a new decision.

rules.name: The Word Not Colour Rule
rules.body: Status is a word, a rule style or a shape, never a colour alone.

rules.name: The Once Rule
rules.body: An animation runs once and never loops. It exists only where the motion is the information or the state change.

dos: Do spend hue on data first: a party's own ink, a semantic ink for its meaning only, series inks for non-party lines.
Do use the one accent for the current place, the selected segment, links, focus, primary buttons and the section dot, and nothing else.
Do pair every colour mark with a word, an abbreviation or a shape.
Do write labels in sentence case at 12-13px, weight 600, and set every figure in tabular numerals.
Do declare a new colour once as light-dark(LIGHT, DARK) and run iei.test.ts, party-ink.test.ts and palette.test.ts after any change to a neutral, an accent or a party ink.
Do say an absence in words ("not loaded", "not reported") at an ink that clears 4.5:1.
Do keep every animation inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
Do put a page's scope in the one-line descriptor under its title.
donts: Don't fill or stroke a seat, bar, ribbon, dot or legend swatch with the accent.
Don't give a page its own hue, or cycle hues by section.
Don't let a party's colour change with rank, count, page or neighbour.
Don't set a label, figure or tag in uppercase, tracked or monospace type.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow above a title; the descriptor goes below it.
Don't add a third radius, a fourth ink tier, or a border to a card in the light theme.
Don't change a shadow on hover or press, or draw a focus ring that is not the 2px accent outline.
Don't print an absence as a bare dash, or a derived figure as if it were announced.
Don't load a webfont, or loop an animation.
